basics.name: Sorawich Chankhiew
basics.label: Backend Software Engineer
basics.summary: Backend software engineer building production systems since 2018, now mainly in Go. At CJ MORE I build services for the POS back-office platform used by stores, distribution centers and head office, and lead three projects: a new asset-tracking service, the in-store print service used in about 1,500 branches, and the team's move to AI-assisted development. Before that I built fintech, healthcare and advertising products with Python, Node.js and React.

work.name: CJ MORE
work.summary: The back-office platform that CJ MORE convenience stores, distribution centers and head office use for stock, campaigns, orders, purchasing, accounting, products and printing: about 21 Go microservices on Kafka, MongoDB and Kubernetes, built by a team of 9 developers, 9 QA engineers and 4 business analysts. 1,400+ commits across 29 repositories since 2023.
highlights: Delivered features across stock, campaigns, orders, purchasing, accounting and products, including multi-round stock recounts, stock transfers with upload validation, campaign transfer-out approvals and reports, SAP file integration over SFTP and a banking partner's mini-ATM API.
Built PDF and Excel reports with Thai fonts, Buddhist-era dates and amounts written out in Thai baht.
Added request and query timeouts to 40+ endpoints across 7 services so slow queries fail fast.

Introduced OpenTelemetry tracing: request context now reaches logs, MongoDB and outbound HTTP calls, and Kafka outbox consumers join the producer's trace. Packaged the setup as a recipe for the other services.

Planned the MongoDB Go driver v2 migration: grouped 21 services by risk and documented critical bugs in the shared library's upgrade branch (a transaction-context leak, a runtime panic and a cursor leak).
Rolled out shared-library upgrades to about 12 services at a time, brought several services' unit-test suites to green, added SonarQube and fixed the shared CI pipelines.

work.name: CJ MORE
work.summary: A new Go service that tracks POS hardware: devices, IMEIs and their movement between branches. I lead the project and built it from zero to production.
highlights: Set up the project from scratch: Docker, GitLab CI/CD with security scans, database migrations and technical docs.
Built a scheduled job that syncs IMEI data from Google BigQuery into MongoDB, then refactored it to run faster.
Built the asset movement and state-history APIs with MongoDB transactions and structured error handling.
Kept lint at zero issues with unit tests, moved to the maintained gomock and MongoDB driver v2, and removed a hard-coded token from the build.

work.name: CJ MORE
work.summary: An ASP.NET Core service that runs on store PCs in every branch (about 1,500) and prints stickers, barcodes and QR labels for the POS web app. I lead the project and am its primary maintainer.
highlights: Built QR-tracking sticker, GS1 DataMatrix and order-shipment label APIs with lot numbers, expiry dates and Thai fonts.
Fixed print jobs that reported success but printed nothing by checking the real printer-queue status, and added a health check.
Added the project's first test suite (47 xUnit tests), label preview and print-queue resource cleanup.
Set the repo up for AI-assisted work: written rules for frozen contracts, an agent that reviews diffs before push, and a sticker-layout skill.

work.name: CJ MORE
work.summary: I lead the team's adoption of AI-assisted development.
highlights: Built and maintain a shared set of 18 Claude Code skills used by 7 teammates, covering unit tests, API specs from source code, QA test cases from a diff and a pre-QA self-review. The unit-test skill cuts the time to write unit tests by about 80%.
Ran AI training for the team.

Built a team knowledge hub with separate lanes for developers, PM/BA and QA. Its generator catalogs 715 endpoints across 21 services with their permissions, so non-developers can explore the system without reading code.
Updated the PDF report code in 7 services using a shared report skill.
Gave knowledge sessions on bitmasks, worker pools and a new error-handling pattern.

highlights: Built the client-facing API that connects the front end to the back-end transfer services.
Integrated the Visa API to process secure credit and debit card transfers reliably.

Scoped new solutions and estimated the resources and timelines needed to deliver them.
Passed the Odoo certification exams.

Refactored and optimized the codebase for performance and maintainability.

Designed the PostgreSQL database.

projects.name: BanFontHub
projects.description: An online store for Thai handwriting fonts, built end to end for a client. Customers try fonts in a live preview, pay by PromptPay QR and get their files by email once an admin approves the payment slip.
highlights: Built the Go (Echo) API on MongoDB and the Next.js storefront and admin, deployed on AWS with font files kept in a private S3 bucket.
Built a live font preview with adjustable size and side-by-side weights, lazy-loading font files so the catalog stays fast.
Automated delivery: approving an order sends a branded email with expiring per-file download links and a one-click ZIP of the whole order.
Added a sales dashboard, bundle promotions and an affiliate program with paid membership tiers and commissions.

projects.name: Scheduled Web Automation Service
projects.description: Scheduled browser automation that completes a recurring multi-step web-form workflow for several users on a third-party, SSO-protected web app with no public API. Running unattended in production since June 2026.
highlights: All code written by Claude Code under a human-in-the-loop process I designed: a hook blocks edits until I approve the plan, every change passes a pytest and ruff gate and a reviewer sub-agent, and every bug fix ships with a regression test.

Built recovery on typed errors (one re-login for an expired session, a fallback engine for a changed page) and a rule never to retry after the final submit, so a failure is flagged as unconfirmed instead of risking a duplicate record.
Encrypted credentials and session cookies at rest, and protected the admin dashboard with CSRF tokens, rate limiting and a security test matrix covering every endpoint for every role.

Cut compute cost by about 87% (≈$24 to ≈$8 a month) by running EC2 only during the daily working windows, and wrote 180+ offline tests plus end-to-end tests in real Chromium against a local fake of the target app.

projects.name: Device Financing Loan Platform
projects.description: A loan management platform for financing Android and iOS phones: partners originate loans for customers, while owners and admins review them, track payments and manage collections. It serves 5 partners financing 100+ devices and THB 1M+ in loans a month. I built features end to end across the Go API and the Next.js web app (180 commits).
highlights: Integrated Android device management so financed phones can be locked and unlocked remotely, with enrollment QR codes for partners, a scheduled job that refreshes them, and credit released only after a lock succeeds.
Built automated LINE payment notifications: a scheduled job with a dry-run mode that sends LINE Flex messages for upcoming due dates, full payment and early settlement.
Added early settlement, multi-slip payment review, claims and device returns to the loan lifecycle.
Built organization onboarding, an investor dashboard, an IT support role and a vendor webhook integration.

awards.title: CJ AI-Native SDLC Hackathon: Highest Score (89/100)
awards.summary: Led AI and development for CJ AI Passport, built by our team in 4 days: an AI-native order-to-cash system (quotations, sales orders, delivery notes and tracking) where AI drafts orders and a person approves them. We built it with a Claude Code setup of 20 skills, 4 sub-agents and a custom MCP server, covering all 8 SDLC phases. It scored 89/100, the highest at the event.
